title: Two for One, 88 Points Apart: Kai Takes Jeanty and Adams, Philly Bets on Justin Jefferson
dek: Alan shipped out 126.4 points of production for 38.4 points of Justin Jefferson, and the model trimmed both teams' title odds by almost exactly the same share.
body: Before week 5, Alan's Team Pillbert and Mekhi's Dawgs made the biggest deal of the young season by sheer volume. Philly sent wide receiver Davante Adams and running back Ashton Jeanty to Kai, and got wide receiver Justin Jefferson back. All three players had spent all four weeks on a roster, so nobody was cashing in a waiver flyer here. This was a 3-1 contender consolidating two starters into one name, and a 1-3 team taking the pile of chips.

The receipts are not close. Adams arrives in Dawgs colors with 62 points, about 15.5 a game, and Jeanty brings 64.4, roughly 16.1 a game. That's 126.4 points going to Mekhi. Jefferson comes to Team Pillbert with 38.4, about 9.6 a game, which means Alan gave up an 88-point season-to-date gap to get him. Even allowing for the fact that you can only start one player per lineup spot, Philly traded two guys outscoring Jefferson for one guy who hasn't.

So why would a first-place team do it? The charitable read is that Alan is buying the player he expects Jefferson to be over the next ten weeks, not the 9.6 a game he's been so far, and betting that one elite receiver beats two good-not-great weekly starters. It also clears a roster spot, which matters for a manager who has been churning his bench like it owes him money. The model, though, wasn't buying the upside pitch: Team Pillbert's title odds slid from 21% to 16%, a five-point drop for a team that only just climbed into the conversation.

Mekhi's odds moved too, from 4% to 3%. That looks like a smaller loss, and in raw terms it is, but here's the strange part: both teams lost roughly a quarter of their title chances. Alan dropped about 24% of his odds, Kai dropped 25%. The model essentially called this a wash in proportion and a lopsided deal in production. On paper, the Dawgs win it, because they kept their losses to a single point while adding 126.4 points of proven output to a roster that badly needed a lift.

The best part is the timing. Week 5 sends Philly into a matchup against Kai's Dawgs, so Jeanty and Adams get to suit up against the manager who shipped them out before Jefferson has played a single down in Pillbert colors. If Jefferson goes off, Alan gets to say he bought the ceiling. If Adams and Jeanty keep producing at their current pace and Mekhi gets to 2-3, this trade gets talked about for the rest of the season, and not in a way Philly will enjoy.

social.author: Dana Whitfield
social.text: Trade details: Team Pillbert sends Davante Adams (62 pts) and Ashton Jeanty (64.4 pts) to Dawgs for Justin Jefferson (38.4 pts). Title odds: Team Pillbert 21% to 16%. Dawgs 4% to 3%.

social.author: Dawgs
social.text: Welcome to the pack, Davante Adams and Ashton Jeanty! 126.4 points of firepower joining up, and their first assignment is a familiar one. See you in week 5, Team Pillbert. 🐾

social.author: Marcus Pell
social.text: Alan gave up 88 more points than he got back and the model cut his odds by a quarter. Mekhi took the production and only lost a point. Jefferson may be the best name in the deal, but the Dawgs won this one on paper.

social.author: Dawg Pound Dre
social.text: Two starters for a guy averaging 9.6 a game? Thank you Philly. Jeanty and Adams vs their old boss in week 5. Kai is cooking.

social.author: Sunday Spreadsheet Sam
social.text: Fun fact: Pillbert lost about 24% of its title odds, Dawgs lost 25%. The model looked at an 88-point gap and said 'eh, same thing.' Somebody explain that to me.
